title: The Golden Rule of Friendship
heading: The Golden Rule of Friendship

sourceRefs.role: core chapter mechanism and one exact quoted line

coreClaim: People like those who make them feel good about themselves.
distinctMechanism: Outward-directed attention creates positive emotional residue that people then associate with you, while ego-focused attention breaks that effect.
requiredAnchors: The Golden Rule of Friendship: if you want people to like you, make them feel good about themselves.
Most people are too focused on themselves and must override ego.
People seek future contact with those who recreate those good feelings.
commonMisreadings: The rule guarantees liking regardless of sincerity.
hardEdgeRequirement: Hard depth must show that the rule collapses when people feel managed, praised mechanically, or used as mirrors for someone else's agenda.
thresholdQuestion: How do you create a good feeling in another person without making the interaction about your skill at doing so?
